call_points.text: Management expects a net positive financial year, with most growth from SSSG plus new-store productivity.
Store rationalisation tail is guided at about 3-4% of stores in a typical year.
Most FY27 gross store openings will start only at the end of Q2 and early Q3.
Franchisee capex is about ₹2,100-2,150 per sq ft in Tier 2/3 cities and ₹2,500 in Tier 1.
Franchisee breakeven revenue per sq ft is about ₹7,000 in Tier 3, ₹8,500 in Tier 2 and ₹10,000-10,500 in Tier 1.
MBO, SIS and e-commerce together are about 5% of revenue, with aggressive growth targets.
Premium brand Twamev outperformed the company on growth; Mohey is growing above the company average.
Gross margin improved to 65.7% in Q1FY27 from 65% in Q4FY26; GST enters the base only from Q3.
Inventory was 34 days for the trailing twelve months to June 2026.
Cash conversion (operating cash flow to PAT, excluding finance income) was about 101% for the twelve months to June 2026.
UAE and North America, the two main international markets, are under pressure from war and tariffs.
September-October may be softer this year as Adhik mass shifts Navratri; November to March is expected to be strong.
Internal research across 8 top states shows store counts starting to fall, with large competitor stores closing.
No SSG target for FY27; management will focus on internal levers like footfalls, conversion and ASP.
Fabric inflation of 50-150 bps on a ₹100 product is expected to be absorbed with minimal gross-margin impact.
FY26 gross margin contraction of ~150 bps was mainly due to GST changes.
Company has historically paid about 50% of profits as dividends; current capital allocation policy is under discussion.
No inorganic acquisition in pipeline; cash is available but nothing in scale exists.
